_comment: Named plugin-profile registry. Resolved by plugin-profiles.mjs into an enabledPlugins map, injected per-dispatch via `claude --settings` (lever-b, highest non-managed precedence) so lane workers run lean while the operator's own ~/.claude stays full. Design: the agent-provider plugin-profiles design spec (specs/design, 2026-07-16). FLOOR is inviolable (harness-operational: dispatch/search/handover). CATALOG is the known plugin universe the resolver sets false for anything a profile does not enable — a COMPLETE map is correct whether Claude Code merges or replaces enabledPlugins. DENY-BY-DEFAULT BEYOND THE CATALOG: the resolver also disables every id passed via opts.installed (the caller's LIVE plugin universe — the spawn scripts pass readEnabledPluginIds over the child's effective config dir + every ancestor settings layer), so a plugin installed/enabled on the machine but absent from CATALOG is still turned off for a lane. Only a CATALOG-ONLY caller (one that passes no opts.installed) retains the staleness gap — such an id stays unmentioned and inherits its enabled state until added to CATALOG (the same class; a pre-commit floor/catalog check is the tracked follow-up). disallowedTools (per-profile, optional) is SCHEMA-ONLY as of task T2.1b — nothing consumes it yet; the producer (a --disallowedTools CLI flag through the claudex builder, via a second resolver export) is T2.3.
_comment_lean_skills_swap: superpowers@claude-plugins-official and mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official are DROPPED from catalog (and lean-skills@himmel added to base, so every profile inherits it) because, measured over 1628 local transcripts, those two always-on plugins carried ~2.2k tok of skill/agent listing into every session for skills almost never invoked (superpowers: 4 invocations ever across 14 skills; mattpocock-skills: zero across 11). lean-skills@himmel vendors verbatim just the subset actually used -- 12 of superpowers' 15 skills (the reference closure of the 4 himmel invokes, plus receiving-code-review) plus grilling from mattpocock/skills and the himmel-authored context7-mcp -- so a session pays for 14 skill listings instead of 26. Per-skill enable/disable does not exist in Claude Code settings, so plugin membership was the only lever; see marketplace/plugins/lean-skills/README.md for the vendoring/drift-detection contract and scripts/lanes/vendored-skill-dupes.mjs (+ himmel-doctor C37) for the duplicate-enablement guard if an adopter turns an upstream plugin back on alongside it.
_comment_gateAllow: /pr-check step 0 now types the no-arg `bash \"$HIMMEL_REPO/scripts/cr/pr-check-step0.sh\"`, which execs the anchor's pr-check-context.sh; it takes the same exact-string carve-out (GATE_ANCHOR_LITERAL_PR_CHECK_STEP0), no tail, so neither lane's auto-mode classifier decides step 0. A council ruling on worker N584: step 0's canonical fence invokes pr-check-context.sh via the literal env-var reference `$HIMMEL_REPO` directly (not the relative `<himmel_dir>` spelling every OTHER scripts/cr/* call uses, since himmel_dir does not exist until this script prints it) — `Bash(bash \"$HIMMEL_REPO/scripts/cr/pr-check-context.sh\")` is an exact-string carve-out in validateGateAllow (GATE_ANCHOR_LITERAL_PR_CHECK_CONTEXT), the same shape as the merge-on-green anchor literal below, admitted so the drifted-branch case (guard-pr-check-literal forces the anchor form whenever the branch's scripts/cr differs from the anchor) reduces to one simple, matchable command instead of the unmatchable compound if/then/else fence; see pr-check.md's restructured step 0. The same ruling also adds two previously-absent scripts, both bare relative literals (documented only via a resolved-path placeholder, never `$HIMMEL_REPO` directly, so they follow the pre-existing GATE_SCRIPT_RE/GATE_EXACT_RE relative pattern, not the anchor-literal one): `scripts/cr/cr-scores.sh` with a `:*` tail (its args vary by call site per docs/configuration.md and the minerva skill) and `scripts/handover/resolve-active-item.sh` as an exact literal (always invoked bare per marketplace/plugins/handover/skills/handover/references/bug-ops.md). Permissions.allow is checked before the auto-mode classifier; deny rules still win and are never emitted or edited here. Guards: merge-on-green checks chief GO, certified green head and unresolved threads; queue-lock checks ownership/release tokens; inbox-send validates a bounded local append; write-verdicts validates verdict inputs; clear-cr-marker limits cleanup to branch markers; panel-first-pass records critic evidence; an operator ruling (2026-09-21: workers may send review diffs to Codex) adds the rest of /pr-check's external-critic steps — docs-audit-panel with a tail, doc-freshness-advisory and `known-findings.sh --diff` as exact literals — and a later change adds /pr-check step 0's himmel-lane entry `bash scripts/cr/pr-check-context.sh` as an exact literal (it runs only in a himmel checkout at its worktree root whose scripts/cr/, scripts/guardrails/lib.sh and scripts/lib/load-dotenv.sh equal the HIMMEL_REPO anchor's byte for byte and mode for mode — the PreToolUse hook guard-pr-check-literal.sh checks that before this rule applies, and that hook is the trust root, not this rule) and another change adds the one var-set the runbook spells for pr-check-env, `bash scripts/cr/pr-check-env.sh CR_CLAUDE_AGENTS` (steps 2.5 / 3.5), as an exact literal under the SAME hook conditions as step 0 (its output steers gate policy; claude-floor-review.sh deliberately has no rule). Every other relative scripts/cr/ literal here is pinned by the same hook to an entry script and scripts/cr/anchor-handoff.sh byte-equal to the anchor's; each entry sources the hand-off first, so the run re-execs the anchor's copy rather than the branch's, and review-round, panel-first-pass and clear-cr-marker refuse a branch other than the one checked out in cwd — and every one is a RELATIVE literal because the matcher compares the command text: /pr-check spells the call `bash scripts/cr/<x>.sh` when step 0's himmel_dir equals its repo, and the absolute `<himmel_dir>` spelling never matched any of these rules; ledger-append validates local evidence rows; check-ci reports forge checks; only the bare `git push` is allowed, in .claude/settings.json; a branch-suffix wildcard stays omitted because it also admits trailing --no-verify and skips the git hooks it relies on. quiet-run itself runs arbitrary argv, so never allow its blanket prefix: only the literal suite label + an enumerated directory + test-*.sh is admitted. A suite run that wants the deterministic rule uses the label suite; any other label simply falls back to today's classifier path — no regression. The matcher's handling of the env prefix and of a tail glob is unproven until the chief's first native --profile worker-impl dispatch. Directory wildcards were dropped because they can absorb a different program before a fake test suffix. Node quiet-run rules are omitted entirely (directory globs/path traversal); node suites remain on the classifier path. scripts/lanes/ has no tracked direct test-*.sh and is omitted. Only the four worker-shaped profiles opt in; operator/user/bare keep their original output. Claudex profile composition is separate; sanitize_settings preserves operator-managed user-scope rules, not these native profile rules. Live proof 2026-09-12 (worker N201, first native --profile worker-impl dispatch): the env-prefix + tail-glob rule shape ran a real suite with no prompt, AND the traversal shape scripts/hooks/test-x/../../evil.sh also ran (rc=127, no denial) — so on this build the allow path does not stop `..` traversal; the structural control is quiet-run.sh's own path guard. The audit (full-file re-audit of the two existing scripts/cr wildcard-tail grants, plus the three scripts #1144 dropped for unconfirmed safety): ledger-append.sh's `:*` tail is safe from code-execution/arbitrary-write/ref-mutation as-is — its `kind` positional is gated to 7 fixed literals (ledger-append.sh:75-78, unknown value exits 2), every write is `fs.appendFileSync` to a ledger path resolved from `$CR_LEDGER` or `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (ledger-append.sh:459), never from argv (and a `CR_LEDGER=... bash scripts/cr/ledger-append.sh` VAR-prefixed spelling does not match this text rule anyway — VAR= drops to the classifier), the main JS block it runs is a static `node - <<'JS'` heredoc with a quoted terminator (ledger-append.sh:477, every caller value passed in as an env var, never interpolated into source) — a second, smaller `node -e` (ledger-append.sh:249) is fed the same way — so no argv byte is ever interpreted as code, argv heads reach `git rev-parse`/`git cat-file` only hex-filtered or via stdin, never as shell text, and `--batch-file` re-validates a row's head/id/branch for presence plus a positive-integer shape on round fields (ledger-append.sh:674-709) — but, unlike the argv `amend` path (ledger-append.sh:307-331), a batch row's severity/verdict/deferred_to are checked for PRESENCE only, not shape (ledger-append.sh:686,698, `f in spec`); batch is `kind=finding` only (amend cannot batch), so this cannot itself forge a disposition, only a badly-shaped one. clear-review-marker.sh's `:*` tail is similarly safe from code-execution/arbitrary-write: its whole CLI surface is one optional branch positional plus `--dry-run`/`-h` (clear-review-marker.sh:131-147; any other flag or a second positional exits 10), the branch value is refused unless it equals `git branch --show-current` (clear-review-marker.sh:197-202) and resolves via `git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/<branch>` (clear-review-marker.sh:205-210), and the ONE destructive op in the file — `rm -f` on the claimed CR-pending marker (clear-review-marker.sh:1369-1393) — runs only after a rename-claim + byte-for-byte content re-check under a branch-scoped mutual-exclusion lock (clear-review-marker.sh:1183-1354); ponytail: the marker-path existence probe (clear-review-marker.sh:186-190, `[ ! -f "$marker" ] && exit 0`) runs BEFORE the branch-identity/ref-verify gate (:197-210), so an arbitrary branch argument is a low-value file-existence oracle ahead of validation — a follow-up tracks reordering it. ponytail: neither grant defends against a worker using its OWN legitimate argv (`avail --status ok --model codex`, `amend --set verdict=disproved`, `amend --set head=<any-hex>`, `amend --set verdict=deferred --set deferred_to=<ticket>`) to self-certify its own CR ledger with the classifier never consulted — inherent to what /pr-check needs these two scripts to do, not a rule-text bug a narrower wildcard could fix (the `kind`/`--set` allowlists are already closed sets) — a follow-up tracks an upgrade path. Both scripts are also TARGETS of guard-pr-check-literal.sh, which denies any command mentioning them that is not one simple command — no `;`, `&`, `|`, backtick, `()`, redirect or embedded newline (guard-pr-check-literal.sh:451-457) — before gateAllow is ever consulted IN A HIMMEL-PROJECT SESSION (the hook is registered only in this repo's own .claude/settings.json / .codex/hooks.json, not at user scope — a worker launched against a non-himmel target repo does not load it), so within a himmel-project session a rider appended past either wildcard tail cannot ride a second command through regardless of what this rule's text alone would match (this is why settings-allow.test.mjs's RIDERS check deliberately excludes `:*` gateAllow rules, and gate-allow-hook-survival.test.mjs exercises the real hook binary directly for both scripts rather than modeling it). The three scripts #1144 dropped stay OUT of gateAllow, now by confirmed audit rather than an unconfirmed guess: handover-bridge.sh's `--notes`/`--bugs` are caller-supplied destination PATHS with no containment check (handover-bridge.sh:36,163-237; scripts/handover/append-cr-findings.sh:17-21 only checks the parent dir exists, never that it sits under a handover root) — a wildcard tail would be an arbitrary-file-write primitive. file-deferred-issues.sh's `--input` reads an arbitrary caller-named file (or stdin) and files matching lines, essentially unfiltered beyond a crude `NIT|LOW|SUGGESTION|IMPROVEMENT|DEFERRED` tag regex, as a live GitHub issue title+body (file-deferred-issues.sh:133-145,371-397) — an externally-visible, hard-to-reverse side effect on attacker-influenceable content. claude-floor-review.sh spawns a fresh BILLED headless claude session via scripts/lib/claude-headless.sh (claude-floor-review.sh:194) — exactly the class of call this file's own CLAUDE.md Claude-invocation-billing rule requires a deliberate, reviewed call site for, never a blanket auto-approval. None of the three has a safe exact-literal shape either — the argument that legitimately varies per call (a handover item path, review text, a branch/base pair) is exactly the part that cannot be pinned — so GATE_SCRIPT_RE/GATE_EXACT_RE correctly reject any shape naming them; they stay on the classifier path (plugin-profiles.test.mjs BAD_GATE_RULES pins this for all three).

_comment_vmLaunchAllow: The ONE rule only the worker-vm profile adds (profile field vmLaunch). It names a station-side script, not ssh: scripts/vm/launch-guest.sh refuses any VM absent from scripts/lib/vms.json, any kind=station entry (win2) and any non-ubuntu guest before it opens a connection, then runs claude on the guest with an explicit --permission-mode acceptEdits and an --allowedTools list, never a skip-permissions flag. A later change widens the same rule: with --lane claudex (only himmel-claudex, a validated --classifier-model and --debug-file required) the script runs scripts/claude-codex on the guest with an explicit --permission-mode auto, still never a skip-permissions flag, after the guest's claude-codex --preflight-only and the Codex bank preflight. A claude launch on this station, a wildcard ssh, or another script does not match the rule. The auto-mode classifier refused every worker that started a claude agent by hand ([Create Unsafe Agents]); an allow rule is checked before the classifier, so this is the sanctioned path.
_comment_chiefAllow: The chief's own go and merge rules, rendered into the chief profile (profile field chiefAllow) the way gateAllow is rendered into a worker's. Relative form only: the chief types `bash scripts/...` from the himmel checkout root, with no cd, timeout, VAR= prefix or absolute path, and a rule matches that text. Each rule is the script path plus `:*`: the script is the gate (the GO writer validates its own argv and refuses a worker, merge-on-green and merge-fork-pr check the GO file and the head), so nothing here is wider than the script path. The chief-only relative merge-on-green rule is NOT a worker rule: a worker's merge is the anchor-absolute twin, and the relative worker rule stays retired. The project file .claude/settings.json holds the go and ready-check rules too; this list is the registry's own copy of the chief's set.
_comment_ruleCapabilities: The capability every himmel-script allow rule grants: go (the GO writer and its verdict plumbing), merge (the merge scripts), ship (pr-check gates, check-ci, quiet-run suites, worker-pr-open and burn), fleet (queue-lock, chief and worker launch, inbox, usage preflight), release (cut-tag), infra (VM and CI-runner control), housekeeping (clean, worktree, doctor, lint). It is the registry that owns the rule set: every rule in gateAllow, vmLaunchAllow and chiefAllow needs an entry (validateRegistry refuses one that has none), and so does every himmel-script rule in .claude/settings.json (settings-allow.test.mjs pins that mirror). Only go and merge are switchable today (a later change filters the render by capability); the rest are tagged and always on.
_comment_himmel_bus: himmel-bus ships no plugin .mcp.json (a plugin-root token cannot be copied into a standalone --mcp-config, refuseIfPluginRootRef), so its stdio server is defined in mcpCatalog. The `${HIMMEL_REPO}` placeholder is resolved by collectMcpServerDefs to the primary checkout's absolute path (a launch with no resolvable checkout refuses), so the server starts from any cwd; mcpAllow names the tools allowed, in both the standalone and plugin-prefixed name forms, for a profile that lists the server. `npm --prefix` runs the plugin's own `start` script, which installs the locked deps once and then execs the server, the self-installing start-script pattern telegram-himmel and luna-correlate use.

worker-impl._comment: Lever 1, audited (2026-10-20, 1376 worker sessions over 14 days). A headed worker re-pays its whole fixed context on every API call of a session that runs for hours, so its budget is the legacy worker target (35000), not the lane-worker default (45000); the calibration audit retains this unmet target because the merged PR bodies cannot attribute three workers to this profile. Do NOT "dedupe" this into lane-impl: a lane worker and a headed worker are different callers, and headed-arm-worker.sh --profile names this one. Plugins = the floor (handover, himmel-ops: its hooks are guards, its skills are used; qmd) plus base's lean-skills (minerva's stages name its skills). nativeDrop turns lean-skills off on the native lane only: native workers invoked it 4 times in 7 days, claudex made 284 of its 534 Skill calls to it, and worker-docs (where spec workers launch) keeps it on every lane. i-have-adhd is in no profile but telegram (its reading-style ruleset, about 2k tokens at SessionStart and again on every compact, was the operator's chief-window style; the chief carries himmel's own 1 KB brief instead). role-requires.mjs names himmel-ops for the worker family: a role with no required plugin gets no skillOverrides and lists 7.4k more first-turn tokens. mcpServers: --strict-mcp-config strips every MCP server not named here, plugin-bundled ones included; qmd is the one MCP server workers call (10 of 1376 sessions). context7 is left out: a worker fetching library docs uses the ctx7 CLI (the find-docs skill) through Bash, which needs no MCP server. MEASURED: dropping the user-level servers saved only 2.5k of first-turn context (73.0k to 70.5k); most of the floor is built-in tool schemas and skill/agent listings. Sibling profile worker-upstream was DROPPED: /drift-fix, /fork-resync and /upstream-file are repo-local .claude/commands/*.md, so it would be a second name for this manifest. worker-docs is back: it is the 200000 docs loop with no guard. An A/B arm needs the plain 200000 ceiling, so on a Sonnet 5.5 launch it runs here, never on worker-impl or worker-eval.
worker-impl._comment_opus: Operator decision 751 (2026-11-07): an Opus 5 worker on the native lane gets an 800000 ceiling and a guard at 700000 tokens. The guard rounds to a whole percent of the 1M window, so share 87 gives ceil(69.6) = 70 percent = 700000; 88 would give 71 percent = 710000. Two real runs at this ceiling each compacted straight after one large read batch (749689 and 678169 by the CLI's own count), so the compaction point is not located; see docs/internals/worker-context-guard.md.

worker-impl._comment_sonnet: Operator ruling 2026-10-30 (option 1, Sonnet workers only): impl runs a 450000 ceiling plus a hand-off at 75 percent. Opus and Fable keep autocompact 200000 with no guard, because the A/B sample was Sonnet only and Phase 1 shows Opus differs after compaction.
worker-impl._comment_share: (chief ruling 2026-11-02): sonnetContextShare 73 makes the guard deny at 33 percent of the 1M window (330000 tokens), not 34 (340000). The hook rounds 75 percent of 450000 = 33.75 up to 34, which left 3158 tokens before the earliest 450000 compaction seen (343158), under the about 7000 a commit, push and CHECKPOINT need; 73 leaves about 13000. It protects the hand-off from a compaction; it does not stop hand-offs.

worker-eval._comment: worker-impl for eval workers, so the operator's per-profile context ruling (2026-10-30) has a name to attach to: eval runs a 450000 ceiling plus compaction on Sonnet. Same plugins, drops and MCP servers as worker-impl; see its _comment.

worker-docs._comment: worker-impl for docs workers, so the operator's per-profile context ruling (2026-10-30) has a name to attach to: docs stays at the 200000 loop on every model. Same plugins, drops and MCP servers as worker-impl except nativeDrop: worker-docs keeps lean-skills on every lane, because spec and design-leg workers launch on it; see worker-impl's _comment.

worker-bus._comment: The first profile on the himmel-bus MCP server; a later change put every headed worker profile on it, so this is now the same manifest as worker-impl, kept as a name existing briefs pass. himmel-bus in mcpServers is what makes headed-arm-worker.sh register the worker on the bus and bind its claude pid. A later change adds the himmel-bus tool allow entries via mcpAllow.

worker-vm._comment: worker-impl plus vmLaunchAllow, the one rule that lets a worker start claude sessions on a registered himmel test VM through scripts/vm/launch-guest.sh. headed-arm-worker.sh refuses this profile for a brief that names no VM from scripts/lib/vms.json. Every other profile stays without the rule.

worker-e2e._comment: Headed e2e worker: worker-impl plus ONE Playwright MCP server, so a worker can drive a browser (the himmelctl config-UI checklist). The server comes from mcpCatalog.playwright (pinned @playwright/mcp, npm registry only, never @latest) and rides --mcp-config under --strict-mcp-config; the playwright@claude-plugins-official plugin is deliberately NOT enabled, because it ships nothing but that same MCP server (no skills, commands or agents) and under strict mode its copy is stripped anyway, so enabling it would add nothing or a second server. Tools therefore appear as mcp__playwright__*, not mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__*. Context cost: the playwright tool schemas add an estimated 3-5k first-turn tokens over worker-impl (code-ui's own estimate, unmeasured here), hence the 40000 budget vs worker-impl's 35000. Use it only for workers that drive a browser; every other worker stays on worker-impl.

telegram._comment: Wired ONLY at the bridge dispatch (scripts/telegram/poller.ts's makeRunFn/runOnce, the sole per-message cold `claude` spawn) — the entry-point inventory found two other Telegram-adjacent spawn sites and both are out of scope: auto-action.ts's dispatchAutoAction spawns no claude at all (it shells out to fixed scripts), and hermes is its own interpreter, dormant, with no plugin-profile seam to wire. enable is obsidian-triage (the actual Telegram workload — clip/harvest/archive/triage/media-enrich commands). claude-obsidian was DROPPED: the bridge's vault-filing prompt (run.ts) named only a vault-local skill or the vault-note plugin, and 147 bridge transcripts show 0 claude-obsidian skill calls and 0 obsidian-vault MCP calls (only obsidian-triage:luna-ingest/telegram-clip ran), while its skill listing costs ~1.6k first-turn tokens; telegram-himmel@himmel is deliberately EXCLUDED even though it is the bridge's own plugin — its .mcp.json defines an MCP server also named telegram (gated by HIMMEL_MCP_TELEGRAM/TELEGRAM_OWN_POLLER) that launches a second poller-adjacent process, which would be self-referential/recursive inside the very session the live poller spawned. luna-correlate@himmel is excluded as unrelated (health-factor correlation, not content work). mcpServers names only qmd — of every plugin in this profile's enable+base+floor union, qmd is the sole one that bundles an MCP server this profile's own plugin set actually needs (of the other marketplace plugins that bundle one, luna-correlate and telegram-himmel are excluded above); --strict-mcp-config then strips every USER-level server (graphify/obsidian-vault/context7/etc.) the bridge never touches. MEASURED (profile-context-probe.mjs): baseline (no --settings, today's live bridge) = 33440-33493 first-turn tokens across runs; telegram profile measured=32541 against contextBudget=45000 (delta -952) — the injected lean set is already BELOW the unleaned baseline, so the win here is deny-by-default correctness (no ambient full ~/.claude leak into an unattended bridge run) rather than a token reduction. The vault-note plugin that had been added here was REMOVED: 0 skill calls in 457 bridge runs over 30 days for ~2.4k-3.5k tokens per spawn; its validate-ai-first write hook now ships in obsidian-triage, and run.ts's filing prompt names obsidian-triage.

No plugins, no MCP servers. drop removes every non-floor id registry.base now carries (lean-skills@himmel as of the lean-skills change -- a relay has no business brainstorming/TDD-ing, it only forwards) so this profile resolves to floor-only, same shape as bare but with gateAllow. console-judge._comment: Design §3.2: a judge session, launched via headed-arm-worker.sh --judge ("the judge is a worker"). drop removes the non-floor id chief-relay drops above (lean-skills@himmel) -- a judge reads and writes a verdict, it does not implement or ship. Deliberately no gateAllow, unlike chief-relay: a judge's few gate-shaped calls (inbox-send.sh, queue-lock.sh, write-verdicts.sh) take the ordinary classifier path rather than being pre-approved wholesale -- its custody rule is "transport is the disk" (a verdict file), not a permission grant, so this name does NOT belong in plugin-profiles.mjs's WORKER_SESSION_PROFILES set (:29, its only reader) and that file is not touched for this profile. mcpServers names only qmd, same reasoning as worker-impl/telegram above: the one MCP tool a judge's evidence-gathering actually needs; graphify/obsidian-vault/context7 are USER-level servers a judge never touches.

release-manager._comment: the release-manager session (headed-arm-worker.sh --profile release-manager). Judge-shaped: drops the implement/review plugins; no gateAllow; jira writes fenced by guard-rm-writes.sh. mcpServers qmd only.

chief._comment: a chief session (chief.sh new/next arm, and a resume of a chief doc). Floor (handover, himmel-ops, qmd) only. gateAllow stays false: the worker-shaped gateAllow rules are for workers, and a chief runs under the operator's own permission config. Not a worker profile, so it is not in plugin-profiles.mjs WORKER_SESSION_PROFILES.
chief._comment_lean: (operator ruling 10-31 LE): the chief launches lean. lean-skills is dropped (0 chief invocations in 231 sessions) and i-have-adhd is in no base, so the chief takes himmel's own 1 KB docs/handover/chief-adhd-brief.md, which headed-arm.sh and chief.sh append with --append-system-prompt-file. denyTools removes the schemas a chief never calls; Artifact is opt-in, and the board stays local. AskUserQuestion and Cron* stay: the chief never calls AskUserQuestion (chief-template.md), and it waits on Cron. Design: the chief lean-profile design spec (specs/design, 2026-10-31).
chief._comment_chiefAllow: chiefAllow renders the registry's chiefAllow list (the chief's go and merge rules) into this profile's permissions.allow; gateAllow stays false, so none of the worker ship-step rules reach a chief.
chief._comment_mcpServers: himmel-bus here is what makes chief.sh register the chief on the bus (role chief) and headed-arm.sh bind its claude pid; without it the edge table (worker to chief) has no chief end and every worker send fails with 'no edge'. A chief launches through headed-arm.sh (and chief.sh's printed line), which passes --mcp-config built from this list plus --strict-mcp-config, so only these servers load; an unresolvable entry refuses the launch.
